title: Talking about hobbies
summary: Asking and talking about hobbies, what you like and prefer, sport and music, what's fun and what's boring.
phrases: What do you like doing in your free time?
My hobbies are reading and swimming. |
I like reading. / I like cooking.
What do you like cooking most?
What kind of music do you like?
I play the guitar. / I play football.
lines: Hi everyone! Welcome to "Daily German Talk"!
Hi, great that you're here.
I'm Anna.
And I'm Ben. We help you practise German.
Exactly! Please subscribe to our channel and give our video a like!
That helps us a lot. Today we're talking about hobbies.
Today's topic is … "Hobbies".
So, Ben, how are you today?
I'm fine, thanks. And you?
Very well. This morning I drank coffee and listened to music. That was nice.
Oh, music, that's a good keyword. What did you do at the weekend?
On Saturday the weather was great. I was in the park. The sun was shining.
That sounds wonderful. On Sunday I watched TV. A lot of it.
Sounds relaxed too.
Yes, very relaxed. But today we're talking about hobbies, right?
Right! Let's start.
So, Anna, what are your hobbies?
I have lots of hobbies. My favourite hobby is reading.
Reading? What do you like reading?
I like reading novels. And sometimes I read newspapers too.
And you, Ben? Do you like reading?
No, reading is boring. I'd rather do sport.
Oh really? What kind of sport do you do?
I play football. Once a week. With my friends.
That's a great hobby. How interesting! Is it tiring?
Yes, very tiring. But it's fun.
Do you only play football?
No. I also like going swimming. In summer I often go to the swimming pool.
Swimming is healthy. I sometimes go swimming, but not often.
And? Do you have another hobby?
Yes, I love music.
Do you listen to music?
I don't just listen to music, I also play an instrument.
That's great! Which instrument do you play?
I play the guitar.
Wow! Can you play me something? Maybe next time?
Maybe. Do you play an instrument?
No. I don't play an instrument. I'm not musical. But I really like listening to music.
What kind of music do you listen to?
I like listening to pop and rock. And you?
I like jazz. Jazz is my favourite genre.
Jazz? That's … surprising.
Why? Isn't jazz good?
Jazz is good, but it's … calm! And you're not always calm.
That's true. But music is relaxing for me.
I see. Tell me … do you like cooking? That's a hobby too, isn't it?
Cooking? Yes, cooking is a hobby. I love cooking.
What do you like cooking most?
I like cooking Italian food. Pasta, pizza.
I like eating pizza. But I don't like cooking.
So what do you do? Do you always eat at a restaurant?
No. That's expensive. I often order food. Or I buy something at the supermarket.
You should cook more. It's not hard.
Maybe. But my hobby is … eating. (grins)
Eating isn't a hobby, Ben!
Why not? I do it very often.
Okay, okay. What's a creative hobby?
Creative … I like taking photos.
That's a nice hobby. What do you photograph?
I photograph the city. Buildings, people, streets. Everything.
Will you show me your photos sometime?
Sure. I have lots of photos on my phone.
Perfect. I sometimes paint.
You paint? I didn't know that. That's very creative.
Yes, I paint with watercolours. It's difficult, but beautiful.
Do you paint people?
No. I paint landscapes. Trees, mountains, the sea.
Very interesting! I can't paint. My pictures are terrible.
Practice makes perfect.
Maybe. I'd rather stick to photography.
Do you like going for walks?
Walks? Yes, I like doing that. Especially in the forest.
That's a relaxing hobby. I also like walking in the forest. The air is fresh.
Exactly. And it's quiet, no stress.
And hobbies at home? Indoor hobbies?
Yes. I like watching films and series.
Ah, a couch potato!
Yes, that's me. And sometimes I play video games.
Video games? Which games do you play?
I like playing adventure games. And you? Do you play video games?
No, that's not my hobby. I find it boring.
Boring? No, it's fun. You have to try it.
Maybe. But I don't have time. I have too many hobbies.
That's true. Reading, playing guitar, painting, cooking, swimming.
Yes, I'm a very busy woman.
What's your hobby for winter?
In winter? I like snowball fights.
Really? That's a funny hobby.
I like skiing. Skiing is my winter hobby.
Skiing? I can't do that. It's too dangerous.
It's not dangerous. It's exciting.
For you maybe. I'd rather stay in my warm house.
You and your warm house.
Yes. My house is my hobby.
Ben, a house isn't a hobby.
Anything can be a hobby.
Okay, philosopher. What's your hobby with friends?
With friends? I play football, you know that. And we often go to the cinema.
Cinema! I like that too. Which films do you like?
I like comedies. Comedies are very funny.
Me too. Let's go to the cinema next week!
Good idea. What's your hobby with your friends?
We meet at a café. We drink coffee and talk.
Talking is a hobby?
Yes, with good friends talking is a wonderful hobby.
That's true. I like talking to you too.
Oh, that's nice. Thanks, Ben.
Tell me, do you like learning languages?
Yes, of course. German isn't my mother tongue.
Really? Your German is perfect.
Learning languages is an important hobby for me.
I'm learning a bit of Spanish. But it's difficult.
Learning languages isn't easy. But it's very useful.
I think so too. By the way … do you like baking?
Yes, I like baking cakes. Chocolate cake is my speciality.
Cake! My favourite cake! Can I try some?
Maybe next time. I don't have any cake here.
What a pity.
Ben, what do you like doing most on a rainy day?
On a rainy day … I read a book.
Wait a moment, you said reading is boring.
Uh, yes, but only sometimes. Sometimes it isn't boring.
You're funny.
Thanks. Being funny is also my hobby.
I believe that straight away.
So, Ben, we've talked about lots of hobbies. Maybe now we can repeat a few important words for our viewers.
Good idea, Anna. That's very useful. Shall we start with the word "Hobby"?
Perfect. So, what is a hobby?
A hobby is something you do in your free time. For example reading, football, music.
Exactly. It's something you do for pleasure, for your free time.
And what's the plural? More than one hobby?
Hobbys. I have lots of hobbies. You have lots of hobbies.
Right, very good! Okay, next important word: Lieblingshobby.
(thinks) Lieblings … Hobby … Ah! Favourite hobby! My favourite hobby is …
Yes. "Lieblings" means "favourite". We can also say: Lieblingsbuch, Lieblingsfilm or Lieblingsessen.
My favourite food is pizza. (laughs)
Of course that's your favourite food. But let's stay on topic. A very, very important expression is: Spaß machen.
That means … to be fun. Or "to make fun"?
Yes. What's fun for you, Ben?
Football is fun, video games are fun.
And what isn't fun?
Tidying up isn't fun. It's boring.
Boring! That's the opposite of Spaß machen! Langweilig means "boring".
Yes. Reading is sometimes boring. (grins at Anna)
Ben! Always the same old song. Reading isn't boring.
Okay, okay. Reading isn't boring. It's … um … relaxing.
Oh, relaxing. That's a fantastic new word. Entspannend means "relaxing".
Yes. Listening to music is relaxing. A walk in the forest is relaxing.
What isn't relaxing?
Football isn't relaxing. Because it's exciting.
Another good word: exciting. Skiing is exciting.
Frightening, for me.
Let's stick to the simple words. Let's do a few more verbs.
What do you do with a book?
I read a book.
What do you do with a film?
I watch a film. Or I look at a film.
Both are correct. What do you do with a guitar?
I play the guitar.
Exactly. You can use "spielen" for instruments and for sport. I play the guitar, I play football.
But careful! You don't say "Ich spiele schwimmen". You say "Ich gehe schwimmen".
Very good, Ben. That's an important difference: "Ich gehe schwimmen".
And what about "treffen"?
That's an important word too.
Yes. I meet my friends.
I meet my friends.
That's a social hobby.
I meet my friends. We go to the cinema. Or we go to a café.
Great! One last word for today: sich interessieren für.
I'm interested … in …
That means: "I am interested in."
What are you interested in, Ben?
I'm interested in photography. And in films. And in pizza.
(sighs, laughing) Always pizza. And I'm interested in art and languages.
We know that.
So. Those were a lot of words: Hobby, Lieblingshobby, Spaß machen, langweilig, entspannend, aufregend, lesen, spielen, treffen, sich interessieren für.
Now it's your turn! Write a sentence with one of these words in the comments.
So, Ben, that was a long, lovely conversation about hobbies.
Yes, really, we talked so much. Now I know that you play the guitar, paint, read and ski.
And I know that you play football, take photos, love films and … are a couch potato.
Hey, that's my relaxing hobby. But seriously, today we practised lots of important sentences.
Let's sum it up once more. What did we practise today?
First: how to ask about a hobby.
The easiest question is: "Was sind deine Hobbys?"
"Was machst du gern in deiner Freizeit?"
Freizeit, that's "free time". And then you can answer: "Meine Hobbys sind …" and list the hobbies.
For example: "Meine Hobbys sind Lesen und Schwimmen."
Or you say "Ich" plus verb plus "gern". Ich lese gern. Ich schwimme gern. Ich spiele gern Fußball.
"Gern" is very, very important. "Ich lese gern" means "I like to read". It shows you enjoy it.
And if you don't like something, you say: "Ich lese nicht gern."
Or: "Ich finde Lesen langweilig." We also learned how to ask for details. For example: "Was liest du gern?"
"Was für Musik hörst du gern?" What kind of music do you like to listen to?
"Welches Instrument spielst du?"
And then we talked about feelings.
"Das macht Spaß!" That's fun.
"Das ist entspannend." That's relaxing.
"Das ist langweilig." That's boring.
"Das ist aufregend." That's exciting.
And I learned that eating maybe isn't an official hobby.
We've settled that. But you're right, we repeated the most important verbs: lesen, spielen, treffen, hören, machen.
I play the guitar. I play football. I meet my friends. I listen to music.
Wonderful. Now it's time for our famous question of the day.
I'm so excited. I love this part.
Today the question of the day isn't just one question, it's three. So you can practise.
Oh, action! Okay. The first question is: What is your favourite hobby?
The second question is: What do you like doing with your friends?
And the third question is: What is a hobby you'd like to learn? A new hobby.
Those are great questions. So, dear viewers: What is your favourite hobby? What do you like doing with your friends?
And what is a hobby you'd like to learn? Please, please write your answers in the comments under this video. We really read every comment.
Yes, we do. And we often reply. We want to learn from you: what are your hobbies? It's so interesting.
Maybe you have a hobby we don't know. Maybe yoga or gardening.
Or programming. Anything is possible. Whatever it is, write to us. You can write in German or in English or in a mix.
The main thing is that you try. And if you need help, just ask us in the comments. We're happy to help.
Before we go, an important reminder: if you liked this video and want to see more German conversations, then …
… click the subscribe button and the "like" heart.
That's very important for our channel. If you subscribe, you won't miss a new lesson.
Next time we'll talk about a new topic. We're going shopping. Going shopping.
Oh yes, we'll learn how to speak German at the supermarket or in a clothes shop.
That'll be fun. So don't miss it, subscribe to the channel.
Thank you so much for learning German with us today. You're great.
We're so proud of you. Keep it up! Remember, every little step counts.
Take care, see you next time.
Bye!
Goodbye!
topics: Your hobbies: what do you do in your free time, what do you like?
Hobbies with friends: what do you do together, where do you go?
Music, films, books: what do you like listening to, watching, reading?
Hobbies in summer and winter: what do you do in each season?

focus.title: Liking to do something
points: It comes after the conjugated verb: Ich lese gern. = I like reading.
Negative: Ich koche nicht gern. = I don't like cooking.
Comparison: gern → lieber → am liebsten: Ich mache lieber Sport. · Was kochst du am liebsten?
In a question: Liest du gern? — answer: Ja, ich lese gern. / Nein, lieber …

focus.title: Playing and going
points: spielen for instruments and ball games: Ich spiele Gitarre. · Ich spiele Fußball. (no article)
For activities you go somewhere to do: gehen + infinitive: Ich gehe schwimmen. · Ich gehe spazieren. · Ich gehe einkaufen.
Common mistake: Ich spiele schwimmen ✗ → Ich gehe schwimmen ✓
in + das = ins: Wir gehen ins Kino. · ins Schwimmbad

focus.title: Favourite …
points: Lieblings- attaches to a noun and makes one word: das Lieblingshobby, das Lieblingsbuch, der Lieblingsfilm, das Lieblingsessen
The new word takes the gender of the last noun: der Film → der Lieblingsfilm
Mein Lieblingshobby ist Lesen. · Was ist dein Lieblingsessen?

focus.title: What kind of …? · Which …?
points: Was für asks about the kind: Was für Musik hörst du? — Pop und Rock.
welcher / welche / welches asks for a choice and is declined like der/die/das: Welches Instrument spielst du? (das Instrument)
Welche Filme magst du? (plural → welche)

focus.title: Being interested in something
points: A reflexive verb: ich interessiere mich · du interessierst dich · er interessiert sich
After für comes the Akkusativ: Ich interessiere mich für den Film / für die Kunst / für das Foto.
Question: Wofür interessierst du dich? = What are you interested in?

focus.title: Verbs that change their vowel
points: With du and er/sie/es the vowel changes: lesen → du liest, er liest · sehen → du siehst
fahren → du fährst · treffen → du triffst, er trifft · essen → du isst
Spaß machen: Das macht Spaß (singular) · Videospiele machen Spaß (plural)
